approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves the molecular formula. After graph checks, identity normalization and duplicate rejection, it evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, and an independent archive keeps the best observation. Each selected transition installs a small, sign-balanced set of changed local motifs, ranked by whole-molecule count change and canonical description. A later neighbor is blocked when opposite inverse signs match the same stored transition.
approach.novelty: Prioritize memory for motifs rooted at the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by the selected transition. A local motif can change merely because an adjacent atom's environment changed; the current count-based ranking can give that surrounding motif a scarce slot while omitting a motif at the actual edit site. The new ranking puts changes supported at those sites first, then uses the Parent's existing ordering. Earlier siblings changed count turnover, occurrence boundaries, ring annotations, score-based credit, matching coverage or overlap retention. None used the concrete edit's atom correspondence to allocate the existing memory slots.

hypothesis: Prioritize a selected transition's globally changed motifs whose signed occurrence changes are supported among the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by that transition, using this binary site-support priority ahead of the Parent's existing rank within its unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif installation.

finding_summary.headline: Direct-site credit redirected 80 evaluations but slightly reduced the panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct edit provenance can redirect scarce memory slots and real evaluations. The unresolved issue is whether the resulting motif restrictions protect useful search behavior. Of the 373 keys added by site priority, 230 later matched a fresh molecule and 60 participated in a bidirectional veto; 105 of the 314 that expired had never matched. Full-stream source improvements increased from 468 to 475 and archive improvements from 238 to 254, while their mean positive gains fell from 0.024350 to 0.022872 and from 0.019744 to 0.018437, respectively. More locally supported credit and more small improvements therefore did not establish the registered panel benefit. A newly admitted sulfur-free aryl-amine molecule reached the DRD2 maximum of 0.949238, showing that useful conventional chemistry was accessible. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur, dense ring systems and undefined stereochemistry elsewhere, especially in the weaker sitagliptin outcome. Root provenance is not a chemical-quality test, and a later shared motif does not demonstrate reversal of the same physical site. The records identify 590 later scored descendants of the 11 changed selected states, but they cannot assign those descendant scores to one credited motif or supply the missing scores and proposals of an alternative walk.
finding_summary.results: On the same 435 selected transitions, the number of installed memory slots supported by a same-sign change at directly edited roots rose from 884 to 1,257 of 1,708 slots, or 51.76% to 73.59%. Retained keys changed at 236 installations; another 64 changed order only. Separate memory histories on the recorded Child walk produced 184 vetoes with the inherited ranking and 117 with site priority: 74 decisions became admissions and seven became additional vetoes. These changes reached 80 actually evaluated molecules across 67 batches, comprising 74 new admissions and six replacement evaluations. Twelve of those molecules improved their source, 68 worsened it, 11 became selected walk states and five improved the archive. All 435 selected-edit replays verified, with no runtime fallback. The three-seed macro mean was 0.520690, compared with 0.521759 for the Parent; the paired change was -0.001069, missing the required +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Mean endpoints improved on four tasks, but the sitagliptin decrease of 0.022009 outweighed those gains, including the DRD2 increase of 0.011290.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich molecules retain aromatic and polar frameworks, but unusual sulfur, reactive bonds and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks have trajectories. Each digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0; aromatic-token occurrence rates, in the supplied task order, are 0.9609, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7747. These are fractions of SMILES containing those tokens, not fractions of aromatic atoms or proof of feasible ring geometry. The molecules span compact fused aromatic carboxamides, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked amines, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. There is real variation across replicas and tasks, but many high-scoring examples are close relatives within these families; molecular uniqueness does not establish broad scaffold exploration. Ordinary amides, ethers, aromatic heterocycles and amines coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and highly constrained ring networks. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre tokens in optimizer proposals. Neutral SMILES can still contain basic amines; absent charge notation does not mean absent ionizability. The Parent comparison shows changes within these families and a notable sulfur-free aryl-amine maximum, without a general resolution of synthetic plausibility. Sizes and structural descriptions below come from passive parsing of the supplied trajectories; scores are recorded observations, not new calculations. The supporting audit, including input hashes and perceived structural descriptors, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-07-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Parsing and ring perception do not establish synthesis, stability, binding or realizable stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals have 21-29 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 46.4. Much of the chemistry retains an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene-like framework connected through a carbonyl to a second aromatic ring, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxymethyl, thiol and halogen substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at 0.39905049777278273 has a recognizable synthetic framework. The maximum at 0.41003927643747895 is instead a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an N-chloro amide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and an amino/chloro carbon. The chemistry remains aromatic/carbonyl-centered, with substantial variation in ring feasibility and substituent reactivity.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-fluoro groups in low-scoring descendants, thiols and benzylic halides introduce reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aromatic/carbonyl framework.
Dense closures and partially dearomatized enlarged rings create uncertain geometry and demanding synthesis; successful parsing is insufficient evidence of accessibility.
missing_features: Coverage of conventional matched carbonyl linkers and substituent patterns remains incomplete around the retained aromatic frameworks; the strong ordinary amide shows that reactive amide chlorination is not required for a high observation.
The bridged and amino/halogen-substituted products lack specified stereochemical identities. The trajectories do not show which configurations, if any, preserve the favorable arrangement.
No unseen optimal scaffold or exact missing target feature can be inferred from these comparisons alone.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich molecules retain aromatic and polar frameworks, but unusual sulfur, reactive bonds and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied tasks have trajectories. Each digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0; aromatic-token occurrence rates, in the supplied task order, are 0.9609, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7747. These are fractions of SMILES containing those tokens, not fractions of aromatic atoms or proof of feasible ring geometry. The molecules span compact fused aromatic carboxamides, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked amines, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. There is real variation across replicas and tasks, but many high-scoring examples are close relatives within these families; molecular uniqueness does not establish broad scaffold exploration. Ordinary amides, ethers, aromatic heterocycles and amines coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and highly constrained ring networks. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre tokens in optimizer proposals. Neutral SMILES can still contain basic amines; absent charge notation does not mean absent ionizability. The Parent comparison shows changes within these families and a notable sulfur-free aryl-amine maximum, without a general resolution of synthetic plausibility. Sizes and structural descriptions below come from passive parsing of the supplied trajectories; scores are recorded observations, not new calculations. The supporting audit, including input hashes and perceived structural descriptors, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-07-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Parsing and ring perception do not establish synthesis, stability, binding or realizable stereochemistry.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves the molecular formula. After graph checks, identity normalization and duplicate rejection, it evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, and an independent archive keeps the best observation. Each selected transition installs a small, sign-balanced set of changed local motifs, ranked by whole-molecule count change and canonical description. A later neighbor is blocked when opposite inverse signs match the same stored transition.
approach.novelty: Prioritize memory for motifs rooted at the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by the selected transition. A local motif can change merely because an adjacent atom's environment changed; the current count-based ranking can give that surrounding motif a scarce slot while omitting a motif at the actual edit site. The new ranking puts changes supported at those sites first, then uses the Parent's existing ordering. Earlier siblings changed count turnover, occurrence boundaries, ring annotations, score-based credit, matching coverage or overlap retention. None used the concrete edit's atom correspondence to allocate the existing memory slots.

research_intent.revisit_rationale: This explicitly revisits the broad expiring inverse-memory cluster, which contains five Knowledge-only observations and no established score benefit for its recent credit/matching interventions. In particular, fractional-turnover ranking changed global occurrence credit but never located a physical edit site; its confirmed activation and negative score effect leave a different explanation open: scarce slots may protect motifs altered only at surrounding roots. The new passive Parent audit directly measures that omission and shows that concrete atom correspondence can replace 345 such slots without changing motif vocabulary, cap, sign allocation, predicate, lifetime or accepted-transition credit. Gain gating and full-signature relaxation also failed their benefit targets, so this experiment does not infer that reducing protection is useful. It tests site-supported selection, which changes conditional decisions in both directions. The Parent stack is unchanged from those recent memory comparisons; the changed causal variable and explicit site-support evidence, rather than a favorable earlier endpoint, are the rationale for this revisit.
